To hear the lark begin his flight,
And singing startle the dull night,
From his watch-tower in the skies,
Till the dappled dawn doth rise.
 Also Ovid, Met. ii 114–15: ‘diffugiunt stellae, quarum agmina cogit/Lucifer et caeli statione novissimus
exit’ (‘The stars all flee away, and the morning star closes their ranks as, last of all, he departs from his

paragraphs.source_en:
But peaceful was the night
Wherein the Prince of Light
His reign of peace upon the earth began:
The winds with wonder whist,
Smoothly the waters kissed,
Whispering new joys to the mild ocean,
Who now hath quite forgot to rave,
While birds of calm sit brooding on the charmed wave.
